chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman leading women in prayer. He said: If they are all together, she may lead them in the supererogatory prayer; but as for the obligatory prayer, then no. And she should not stand in front of them; rather, she stands in the middle among them.

key_terms.النِّسَاءَ: women being led in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَؤُمُّ: leads in salat (prayer) as the Imam
key_terms.تَتَقَدَّمُهُنَّ: stands ahead of them as the leader
key_terms.وَسَطًا: in the middle position among them

ai.seo_question: Can a woman lead other women in salat (prayer), and where should she stand?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman leading other women in salat (prayer). It states that she may lead them in supererogatory prayer, but not in the obligatory prayer, and that when she leads, she does not stand ahead of them but stands in the middle among them.
